en: The Banaue Rice Terraces in the Philippines act as giant inclined planes to slow down water flowing down the mountains.
Apollo 15 astronaut David Scott proved gravity accelerates all objects equally by dropping a hammer and feather on the Moon.
The SCMaglev train in Japan uses powerful electromagnets to float above the tracks, eliminating wheel friction.
Alessandro Volta created the voltaic pile, the world's first electrical battery, by stacking alternating discs of zinc and copper.
The Philippine firefly, Pteroptyx malaccae, produces cold light through a chemical reaction called bioluminescence to attract mates.
A sperm whale produces the loudest biological sounds on Earth, emitting clicking noises that reach 230 decibels underwater.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay generates electricity by harnessing the Earth's internal heat from underground steam.
Water stored high behind the Magat Dam in Isabela possesses gravitational potential energy that turns into kinetic energy.
Christopher Cockerell invented the hovercraft, which uses a cushion of air to drastically reduce surface friction.
Stephenson's Rocket, an early steam locomotive, converted thermal energy from burning coal into mechanical motion.
The Bukidnon Solar Power Plant uses photovoltaic cells to convert radiant energy from the Sun into electricity.
Alexander Graham Bell's first telephone converted sound energy into electrical signals to transmit speech over wires.
